content: The test image shows corn kernels with pinkish/salmon coloration and white fuzzy mycelium — this points to an ear rot. Let me compare the relevant reference images.

**Test image analysis:**
- Corn kernels, pale pinkish/salmon color
- Dense white cottony mycelium visible between and around kernels
- No green/black spores (rules out Aspergillus)
- Kernels are distinctly pinkish, not tan/brown (distinguishes from Diplodia)

**Reference comparison:**
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Yellow kernels + green/olive mold — no match
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: Tan/brown kernels + white mycelium — similar texture but wrong kernel color
- **Fusarium**: White/pink mycelium on yellow kernels — partial match
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella** reference images showed stalk symptoms, but Gibberella ear rot is classically characterized by **pink/salmon kernel discoloration** with white-to-pink mycelium — this strongly matches the test image

The pinkish/salmon kernel coloration is the key diagnostic feature. Gibberella ear rot (caused by *Fusarium graminearum*) produces exactly this pink-to-red discoloration of kernels with cottony white mycelium. Diplodia produces tan/gray kernels and Aspergillus produces yellow kernels with green spores.
